analysis.title: Permian Resources Corp. (PR): First Take: Strong 3Q26 FCF Beat Versus GS and Consensus; Focus on $1.03B Ridge Runner II Acquisition
key_insights: PR reported 3Q26 free cash flow of $846 mn against GS and consensus estimates of $769 mn and $748 mn, a beat of 10% and 13%.
3Q26 adjusted EBITDA was $1.43 bn, 7% above both GS ($1.34 bn) and consensus ($1.34 bn). Capex of $518 mn was 3% above GS ($504 mn) and 4% above consensus ($500 mn).
Total production was 458 Mboe/d against GS at 427 and consensus at 434. Oil volumes were 208 Mbbls/d, 2% above both. Natural gas was 787 Mmcf/d, 12% above GS, and NGLs were 118 Mbbls/d, 11% above GS.

PR raised 2026 oil production guidance to about 203 Mbo/d at the midpoint from about 199 Mbo/d, above GS and consensus at 200 Mbo/d. Total production guidance rose to 415-445 Mboe/d from 400-430 Mboe/d.

2026 capital spending guidance rose to $1.98-$2.08 bn from $1.90-$2.00 bn, in line with GS at $1.99 bn and consensus at $1.98 bn. Total cash costs guidance was held at about $7.65/boe at the midpoint, against a GS estimate of $7.46/boe.

PR is acquiring about 24k net acres, about 9k net royalty acres and about 13 Mboe/d of production at a roughly 45% oil cut for about $1.15 bn in total. This includes the $1.03 bn purchase of Ridge Runner Resources II, LLC and its affiliated royalty company.
PR says the Ridge Runner assets have a weighted average breakeven of about $35/bbl and expects the deal to add to cash flow, FCF and NAV per share in the short and long term.

The 3Q26 transactions were funded with cash on hand and commercial paper. PR estimates net debt to LQA EBITDAX below 0.5x at year-end 2026. Net debt was about $3.00 bn at 3Q26 end against $2.89 bn at 2Q26 end.

The Ridge Runner deal carries up to $125 mn of contingent cash payments. They are paid quarterly in 2027 and 2028 and depend on average WTI prices in each quarter relative to $70/bbl and $80/bbl thresholds.

GS rates PR Buy with a 12-month price target of $29, 29.3% above the $22.43 close on 4 Nov 2026. The target uses a 12.5% FCF yield on 2027/2028 estimates at $80/$75 Brent and $3.50 Henry Hub gas, weighted 85% to a fundamental value of about $28 and 15% to an M&A value of about $32.

GS key questions for the 10 AM ET call cover 2027 activity and oil volume trajectory, capital efficiency, 2027 gas sales after the recovery in Waha pricing, how Ridge Runner II competes for capital within the portfolio, and near-term capital allocation priorities.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps its Buy and $29 target after a 3Q26 FCF beat and raised 2026 production guidance. The target is unchanged from the 26-Oct-26 level.

earnings_insights: PR 3Q26 reported 11/4: free cash flow $846 mn vs GS est $769 mn and consensus est $748 mn.
PR 3Q26 reported 11/4: adjusted EBITDA $1,429 mn vs GS est $1,337 mn and consensus est $1,335 mn. Operating cash flow $1,364 mn vs GS est $1,274 mn and consensus est $1,248 mn.
PR 3Q26 reported 11/4: adjusted EPS $0.69 vs GS est $0.65 and consensus est $0.61. Cash flow per share $1.59 vs GS est $1.54 and consensus est $1.48.
PR 3Q26 reported 11/4: capex $518 mn vs GS est $504 mn and consensus est $500 mn.

PR 3Q26 reported 11/4: realized oil price $79.96/bbl vs GS est $78.53/bbl. Production costs $6.32/boe vs GS est $6.64, production taxes $3.61 vs GS est $3.29, G&A $1.16 vs GS est $1.31, total cash costs $11.09 vs GS est $11.24, all-in costs $25.34 vs GS est $25.71.

PR 2026 guidance: oil about 203 Mbo/d at the midpoint (prior about 199, GS est 200, consensus est 200), total production 415-445 Mboe/d (prior 400-430, GS est 412, consensus est 416), capex $1.98-$2.08 bn (prior $1.90-$2.00 bn, GS est $1.99 bn, consensus est $1.98 bn), total cash costs about $7.65/boe at the midpoint (GS est $7.46).

GS quarterly EPS estimates for PR: $0.93 for 6/26 (reported), $0.65 for 9/26E, $0.79 for 12/26E and $0.65 for 3/27E. The 9/26E figure was the estimate before the 11/4 print, which came in at $0.69 adjusted. GS annual EPS estimates are $2.43 for 2026E, $2.59 for 2027E and $2.26 for 2028E.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Contingent payments of up to $125 mn depend on each quarter's average WTI price relative to these thresholds, so the deal's total cost rises with oil prices.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS fundamental valuation of PR uses these Brent prices. The M&A valuation uses $85 and $80.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS fundamental valuation uses $3.50 for both years. The M&A valuation uses $3.75 for both years.

risk_factors: GS lists key risks to PR as costs, well results, commodity price volatility and government pronouncements.
Ridge Runner contingent payments of up to $125 mn rise if WTI averages above the $70/bbl and $80/bbl thresholds in 2027 and 2028.
Net debt rose to about $3.00 bn at 3Q26 end from $2.89 bn at 2Q26 end, with the acquisition funded partly by commercial paper.
